[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
James Glasgow is said to have been born about 1700 and has been attached as a son of [[Glasgow-1073|John Glasgow]] and [[Scott-40313|Margaret Scott]]. However, the parish-register citation previously used for this claim records the baptism of a son named '''John Glasgow''', not James. A source specifically identifying James and establishing his parentage is required.

=== Incorrect identification in the Crawfurd papers ===

This profile previously claimed that James Glasgow had settled in Ireland by 1720 and had received money there through Robert Glasgow, factor at Kilbirnie. Those claims resulted from a misidentification of documents connected with the fraudulent Crawfurd peerage claim.

A genuine letter dated '''23 March 1720''' was addressed by George, Viscount Garnock, to '''Robert Glasgow''', his factor. Four lines were subsequently inserted into the letter by the forger '''William Bradley'''. The inserted passage referred to a bill for “my brother James” in Ireland. The James intended by the fabrication was the Viscount’s brother, '''James Crawfurd''', not James Glasgow.<ref name="Dobie1831">James Dobie, ''Examination of the Claim of John Lindsay Crawfurd, to the Titles and Estates of Crawfurd and Lindsay'' (Edinburgh: William Blackwood; London: Thomas Cadell, 1831), pp. 102–104, [https://deriv.nls.uk/dcn23/9537/95375734.23.pdf National Library of Scotland digital copy].</ref>

The alleged financial record dated '''3 March 1725''' likewise does not concern James Glasgow. The inserted account entry named '''James Crawfurd''' and purported to record a remittance through Arthur Dawson of Dublin. Dobie identified both this account entry and the corresponding receipt as forgeries executed by Bradley.<ref name="Dobie1831" />

There is therefore no evidence in these documents that James Glasgow settled in Ireland, received a £25 sterling remittance, conducted business there, or maintained financial connections between Ireland and Scotland. The earlier statements based on these records should not be relied upon.

A genuine letter dated 22 November 1722 was sent by [[Glasgow-1075|Robert Glasgow]] at Paddockholm to '''James Glasgow, student of divinity at Glasgow, his brother'''.<ref>National Records of Scotland, RH15/120/178, letter from Robert Glasgow, Paddockholm, to his brother James Glasgow, student of divinity at Glasgow, 22 November 1722, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=RH15%2F120%2F178 catalogue description].</ref> This independently identifies an adult James in the Kilbirnie family and places him at Glasgow as a divinity student. It does not give his age or parents, and it supplies no evidence that he was a captain or later lived in Ireland.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1073]] is assessed at 99% (proved). The Kilbirnie OPR entry of 17 March 1700 (596,10/30,FR27) names James’s parents John Glasgow and Margaret Scot. Fasti VIII p35 independently includes the Castle minister James among Rev John’s children by Margaret Scott, agreeing with his Glasgow MA and 1738 ordination chronology.

Confident for Rev John-1073 as the Castle minister’s father. The stale captured John-child citation and the rejected Crawfurd Irish pedigree do not supersede this combined maintained evidence.

Next useful test: Use the original OPR and Fasti account if a competing James minister is suggested.

Source basis already held: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3585861&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564-1929: James Glasgow, 17 Mar 1700, record SCOT/OPR/BAP/3585861]; [https://electricscotland.com/bible/fastiecclesiaesc03scot.pdf p. 103 (https://electricscotland.com/bible/fastiecclesiaesc03scot.pdf).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


[[Glasgow-1077|John Glasgow MA (1690–1764)]] is reported to have had a brother named James who worked as a shipwright in Irvine. A Captain James Glasgow, described as an Irvine shipmaster, may also be mentioned in records dating from about 1740. Further evidence is required to establish whether either reference concerns the James represented by this profile.

The reference to the ''Decennial Indexes to the Services of Heirs in Scotland, 1700–1859'' requires a full citation and an explanation of the relevant entry before it can support any identification.

=== Minister of Edinburgh Castle ===
James graduated M.A. at the University of Glasgow on 10 March 1718.<ref name="FastiCastle">Hew Scott, ''Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae'', new edition, vol. 1 (Edinburgh, 1915), Edinburgh Castle, entry for James Glasgow ([https://archive.org/details/fastiecclesiaesc01scot Internet Archive]).</ref> On 7 July 1737 George II commissioned him minister of Edinburgh Castle. The royal commission appointing James Glasgow, styled Clerk, chaplain to the garrison was read in the Presbytery of Edinburgh in October 1737.<ref>''The Daily Gazetteer'' (London), 3 November 1737, p. 1, Edinburgh report of 21 October ([https://www.newspapers.com/image/1142270617/ Newspapers.com image 1142270617]).</ref> As a probationer he was ordained minister of the Castle on Tuesday 14 February 1738.<ref>''The Daily Gazetteer'' (London), 23 February 1738, p. 1, Edinburgh report of 16 February ([https://www.newspapers.com/image/1142271259/ Newspapers.com image 1142271259]).</ref><ref name="FastiCastle" /> He died on 9 February 1746, aged about 48, while minister of the Castle.<ref name="FastiCastle" />

The Fasti account of his father's parish of Kilbirnie names him among the children of [[Glasgow-1073|Rev. John Glasgow]] and his second wife [[Scott-40313|Margaret Scott]]: "James, min. of Edinburgh Castle; Margaret; William; Samuel; Janet ... Elizabeth; Jean".<ref name="FastiKilbirnie">Hew Scott, ''Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae'', new edition, vol. 3 (Edinburgh, 1920), Kilbirnie, entry for John Glasgow ([https://archive.org/details/fastiecclesiaesc03scot Internet Archive]).</ref> This agrees with his baptism at Kilbirnie on 17 March 1700 as son of John Glasgow and Margaret Scot, and with the 1722 letter from his half-brother [[Glasgow-1075|Robert Glasgow]] of Paddockholm to "his brother James Glasgow, student of divinity at Glasgow".
